summary: Wooden lighthouse on Sea Bird Point, lit 8 April 1886 for Haro Strait; Mary Ann Croft kept it from 1902; the present tower dates from the 1970s.

structures.type: square pyramidal wooden tower with metal lantern, joined to a one-and-a-half-storey keepers' dwelling
structures.note: 41 ft to the vane (LighthouseFriends). Its later history is not given.

structures.type: lantern on the roof of a two-storey keepers' dwelling (the second light)
structures.note: Date not given in sources read; the dwelling housed keepers until January 1997.

access.note: Provincial marine park; grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Chance Heritage Trust: no protected landing for boats; access mostly by sea kayak.

keepers.name: Patrick Mickey

wrecks.outcome: Caught fire near the island, bound Victoria to the Fraser River; her captain grounded her on the eastern point; later floated (LighthouseFriends)
Passed the island at about midnight in fog while the station's fog signal was silent. No damage recorded in the source read; marine agent James Gaudin on board.

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends: the dwelling 'continued to house keepers until the station was de-staffed in January 1997'. The station record's 1996 date is not confirmed by a source read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1886 is the first light (wooden tower, first exhibited 8 April 1886). The record's 1970 first light fits the present 1970s tower, not the station's start.
The light was not discontinued; the record's 'inactive' conflicts with the Coast Guard's current list entry, which gives a live characteristic (Fl W 5s). Status treated as active.
The Department's list gives 1 April 1902; LighthouseFriends gives 9 April 1902. The Department's entry is cited here, the difference is noted.

notes_for_editor: CONFLICTS: (1) Croft's appointment: Department list gives 1 April 1902 with a salary of $960 (matched by column position in a scanned table, OCR 'M. A. Croft April 1, 1902.. 960 00'); LighthouseFriends gives 9 April 1902. Story gives the Department's date and notes LF's. (2) The Brinn appointment (14 June 1886, $900) comes from the station row of the 1901 list; the names in the list are alphabetical, so the match of name to station is by LighthouseFriends, not by position. (3) Tower dates: the station record gives 1958 for the earlier tower and 1970 first light; LighthouseFriends says the present tower dates from the 1970s. No source read dates the 1958 tower. (4) De-staffing: LighthouseFriends January 1997; station record 1996. (5) Wikipedia places the light on Pandora Hill; LighthouseFriends and the Coast Guard list put it at Sea Bird Point. Wikipedia not cited. (6) The Chance Heritage Trust page repeats LighthouseFriends' text nearly word for word; it is cited only for the 'no protected landing' line, which is not in LighthouseFriends. (7) Keepers after 1932 come from LighthouseFriends only; the corpus of Department reports ends in 1924. (8) The 1914 diaphone, the 1885 contract, the 1886 first exhibition, the 1889-90 fog alarm and the 1892 Premier passage are LighthouseFriends' accounts; the Department reports for those years are not in the corpus. (9) 'Canada's first female lightkeeper' is LighthouseFriends' claim, not checked. (10) Post-1960 keepers (Stout, Fox, Nelson, Nutall, Carr, Mickey, Pike) are named as LighthouseFriends prints them, with no further personal detail. (11) Sea Bird Point is named in the 1858 account only through LighthouseFriends. (12) The Department list's Discovery Island row shows the station's appointment date and salary, not Brinn's name. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-28 (independent checker): all 37 original quotes were found on the first run. The Department's 1 April 1902 date and $960 salary for M. A. Croft are printed in the same row layout in four separate Department lists (1909, 1910, 1914, 1915 volumes of the corpus, checked by text, not by page image), so the match is consistent across years; the page image was not viewed. The 14 June 1886 / $900 Discovery Island row in the 1901 list is read by text, not by page image. Story revised: the 'Provincial marine park' line is now sourced to the Chance Heritage Trust (its 'provincial park' wording), not LighthouseFriends; the Haro Strait / Strait of Juan de Fuca junction is footnoted to Chance; the claim that Mary Ann Croft kept the station 'with an assistant' after 1901 is removed (the assistant is only a proposal in Agent Gaudin's letter, as LighthouseFriends quotes it); the Chance wording is rewritten in our own words; metres added first for Canadian heights and distances.
